header:
Date: 2026-09-10 | Time: 15:30 PDT | Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE); Lena Cho (Redwood SE); Maya Grant (Redwood CSM); Jared Ortiz (Peregrine CTO); Priya Shah (Head Eng); Luis Ramirez (Infra)
Recording: Active
Meeting recorded via Fireflies.ai
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — is this still a good time? ...
[00:00:18] Jared Ortiz: Yep, we’re good. Sorry running a bit behind. Thanks for doing the immersion today, looking forward to the plan.
[00:00:28] Samir Patel: Cool. I'll do a 5-min framing then Lena will go into VPC and security and Maya will cover the onboarding runbook. Then we can do Q&A and next steps. Sound alright? 
[00:00:45] Priya Shah: Yep that's perfect.
[00:01:10] Samir Patel: Quick wins — our typical kickoff is: sandbox tenant, basic integration for routing inference calls, run two benchmarks (latency and cost), then a 2-week pilot. Success criteria you mentioned in emails were latency under p95 400ms and cost target per 1k tokens under your threshold — remind me that threshold again? 
[00:01:34] Priya Shah: We were thinking p95 under 350ms and cost under $0.50 per 1k tokens for our high-throughput flows. The 350 number is the one that triggers further exec sign-off.
[00:01:51] Samir Patel: Got it. We'll try to hit p95 <350ms. For that we'll recommend Dedicated for steady traffic, or Hosted with burst if you want to avoid long-term commit. Lena, want to dig into the connectivity options? 
[00:02:10] Lena Cho: Sure. So two paths: Redwood Hosted API (fastest to ship, TLS, token auth) or Redwood Private — VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink — that gives you control of egress, KMS integration, and no token egress. For Peregrine's compliance ask you'll probably want the VPC path. Note: VPC requires firewall rule egress to our IPs and a short security onboarding window.
[00:02:45] Luis Ramirez: Slight stutter — the PrivateLink option, does it keep all traffic within our account, or is there still a control-plane call to Redwood? 
[00:02:56] Lena Cho: There is a light control-plane handshake for metrics/rollouts, but payloads can be routed directly to your dedicated runtime. We can also offer fully air-gapped options if you need on-prem packaging but that takes longer.
[00:03:20] Priya Shah: We probably won't do on-prem initially. We want VPC peering + KMS. Also curious about model pinning and rollouts — how do you handle rollback if a model regression occurs? 
[00:03:35] Maya Grant: We do staged rollouts — canary percent, A/B routing, and automated rollback based on evals or latency/error spikes. You can pin customers to model versions; we also expose token-level cost dashboards so you can see unit economics per model.
[00:03:56] Jared Ortiz: Nice. On the benchmarks: we need both cold-start and steady-state. How does redwood handle KV cache priming and key-value cache — I keep seeing "KV cash" in our notes — I mean cache. 
[00:04:10] Lena Cho: Yeah KV cache — we support prefix caching and warmup API. For steady-state we recommend a short priming run and enabling prefix cache; that reduces per-token compute by reusing KV. Also quantized variants reduce memory and cost but can affect output quality; we can recommend a quantization profile for your use-case.
[00:04:35] Luis Ramirez: Any limitations on sequence length? Some of our flows hit 4k tokens intermittently. 
[00:04:41] Lena Cho: We support up to 8k on our larger runtime profiles. For cost and latency you want to avoid very long sequences if low latency is required — batching tends to increase throughput but adds latency; continuous batching is workload-aware in the runtime.
[00:05:00] Priya Shah: On auth/SSO — we want to map SAML groups to RBAC roles so our Managed Ops team can see only certain routes. Supported? 
[00:05:12] Maya Grant: Yes — SAML/SSO with SCIM user provisioning; role-based access control per route and per environment. We log token-level actions to audit logs (retention options available).
[00:05:28] Jared Ortiz: For compliance: SOC2, ISO, and KMS integration — do you have a security pack? 
[00:05:35] Lena Cho: Yes. We have a security package: SOC 2 Type II report, ISO docs, and a KMS/HSM integration guide. I'll share the links after the call. Note: some of the documents are redacted for PII but we'll schedule a secure transfer.
[00:05:51] Samir Patel: I'll send the security artifacts in a secure share. Also will include the standard network egress CIDRs. 
[00:05:57] Priya Shah: Pricing — we've got a cap in the pilot so need to see an initial estimate. 
[00:06:05] Samir Patel: We'll draft an estimated run-rate for the pilot using your expected qps and token distribution. Can you confirm expected peak qps and percent of long sequences? 
[00:06:20] Priya Shah: Peak around 120 rps for the next quarter test, with ~10% long (>2k token) requests.
[00:06:28] Samir Patel: Perfect — that'll help us size dedicated capacity vs hosted burst. For pilot we usually recommend a small dedicated pool or hosted with autoscaling. Lena: any setup time estimates? 
[00:06:40] Lena Cho: For Hosted it's minutes. For VPC peering + KMS typically 7–10 business days including firewall approvals and cert exchange; if Peregrine provides network diagrams and security contacts we'll start immediately.
[00:06:56] Luis Ramirez: We can get the network diagram today. One ask from infra: can we run a perf benchmark inside our VPC before we commit? 
[00:07:05] Lena Cho: Yes — we provide a sandbox runtime you can call from your VPC for benchmarking; we'll supply test endpoints and a small harness script.
[00:07:14] Priya Shah: Great. Ops question: observability — do you export traces to our X-Ray/Datadog or only to Redwood console? 
[00:07:23] Maya Grant: We push traces to your preferred tracing backend (supported: Datadog, NewRelic, AWS X-Ray) and the Redwood Console will provide per-route breakdowns. Metric export via prometheus pushgateway or cloudwatch is possible too.
[00:07:41] Jared Ortiz: One more — who owns the escallation for production incidents? 
[00:07:45] Samir Patel: Redwood provides a primary on-call for the runtime, with an SLA path. We'll provide the on-call contacts in the SOW and Cx will be routed through Maya as CSM.
[00:07:58] Priya Shah: Cool. Timeline recap? 
[00:08:02] Maya Grant: Proposed timeline: this week — get network diagram & fill security intake; next week — Redwood provisions sandbox, we run benchmarks; week after — pilot kickoff (2 weeks); after pilot — review and production roll. Aim for production mid-Oct if pilot goes well.
[00:08:21] Priya Shah: That fits our target.
[00:08:34] Samir Patel: Let's capture next steps — I'll send pricing and SOW, Lena will share security pack and sandbox setup, Maya will create the tenant and invite the users. We'll reconvene for a security deep-dive next Thu. 
[00:08:53] Jared Ortiz: Sounds good. A couple of small clarifications on the ramp; will you include example payload sizes and sample prompts for benchmarking? 
[00:09:02] Lena Cho: Yes, we'll include sample payloads and a harness script. 
[00:09:10] Priya Shah: Thanks all. Quick note — we might have legal review in parallel; procurement will reach out if needed.
[00:09:18] Samir Patel: Noted. Any other questions? 
[00:09:24] Luis Ramirez: None from me.
[00:09:26] Maya Grant: Ok wrapping — I'll send calendar invite for the security deep-dive and attach the intake form. 
[00:09:34] Samir Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts within 48 hours. End.
[00:09:40] Speaker 2: (inaudible) okay bye.

Summary: Short onboarding immersion focused on network/VPC connectivity, SOC2/KMS security artifacts, pilot sizing with peak ~120 rps, success criteria p95 <350ms, and a 2-week pilot target week of 2026-09-20. Action items assigned. Shared artifacts: security pack (link to secure share), sandbox setup guide (link), pricing estimate (to be sent).
